title: CHAPTER 1: BASICS OF ECONOMICS
content:
👋 ሰላም! ውድ የEthioFresh ቤተሰቦች! Chapter 1ን ሙሉ በሙሉ ለማጠናቀቅ ዝግጁ ናችሁ? ✋ ዛሬ ደግሞ የቻፕተሩን የመጨረሻ እና በጣም ሳቢ ክፍሎች (Sections 1.6 & 1.7) ይዘንላችሁ መጥተናል!

በዚህ ክፍል፦ Economic Systems (Capitalist, Command, Mixed Systems)፣ ጥቅሞቻቸውና ጉዳቶቻቸው፣ Decision Making Units (Households, Firms, Government) እና በሁለትና ሶስት ሴክተሮች መካከል ያለውን የ Circular Flow Model ሁለቱንም ፍሰቶች (Real & Money Flows) በግልፅና በፍፁም በማይሰለች አቀራረብ እንመለከታለን። እስከ መጨረሻው አብራችሁን ሁኑ! 👇👇👇


1.6 Economic Systems

The way a society tries to answer the fundamental economic questions (What, How, and For Whom to produce) is summarized by a concept known as an economic system.

Definition: An economic system is a set of organizational and institutional arrangements established to answer the basic economic questions. Customarily, we can identify three major types of economic systems:
1. Capitalist Economy (Free Market System)
2. Command Economy (Socialist System)
3. Mixed Economy

👉 የኢኮኖሚ ስርዓት (Economic System) ምንድን ነው? :
ማንኛውም ሀገር ወይም ህብረተሰብ ለሶስቱ መሠረታዊ የኢኮኖሚ ጥያቄዎች (ምን፣ እንዴት እና ለማን ይመረት?) መልስ ለመስጠት የሚከተለው ድርጅታዊና ህጋዊ አሰራር Economic System ይባላል። በዓለማችን ላይ በዋናነት 3 የኢኮኖሚ ስርዓቶች አሉ።


1.6.1 Capitalist Economy (Capitalism / Free Market / Laissez-faire)

Capitalism is the oldest formal economic system in the world, becoming widespread in the middle of the 19th century. In this economic system, all means of production are privately owned, and production takes place at the initiative of individual private entrepreneurs who work mainly for private profit. Government intervention in the economy is minimal.

Main Features of Capitalist Economy:
• The right to private property: Economic or productive factors such as land, factories, machinery, and mines are under private ownership.
• Freedom of choice by consumers: Consumers can buy the goods and services that suit their tastes and preferences (known as consumer sovereignty).
• Profit motive: Entrepreneurs are guided by the motive of profit-making in their productive activities.
• Competition: Competition exists among sellers/producers to attract customers, among buyers to obtain goods, among workers to get jobs, and among employers to get workers and investment funds.
• Price mechanism: All basic economic problems are solved through the market forces of supply and demand (the price mechanism).
• Minor role of government: The government does not interfere in day-to-day economic activities and confines itself to defense, maintenance of law and order.
• Self-interest: Each individual is guided by self-interest and motivated by the desire for economic gain.

Disadvantages / Drawbacks of Capitalism:
• Inequality of income: Wide economic gap between the rich and the poor.
• Existence of negative externalities: Profit maximization may lead to harms like pollution imposed on third parties.
• Unbalanced economic activity: Development can occur unevenly across geographic regions or social sectors.
• Exploitation of labor: Common practice of paying low wages to maximize profits.

Advantages of Capitalist Economy:
• Flexibility and adaptability: Adapts successfully to changing environments.
• Decentralization of economic power: Prevents concentration of economic decision-making in a single central authority.
• Increase in per-capita income: Rapid growth leads to higher standards of living.
• Optimum utilization of resources: High efficiency driven by innovation and technological progress.
• New types of consumer goods: Wide variety of goods developed at large scale.

👉 ካፒታሊዝም (Capitalist Economy) :
• ዋና መገለጫዎች፦ የግል ሀብት ንብረት ማፍራት ይፈቀዳል፤ መንግስት በገበያ ውስጥ ጣልቃ አይገባም (Laissez-faire)፤ ምርት የሚመረተው ለትርፍ ሲባል ነው፤ ዋጋ የሚወሰነው በገበያ ፍላጎትና አቅርቦት (Price Mechanism) ነው።
• ጥቅሞቹ፦ የፈጠራ ስራና ቴክኖሎጂ ይስፋፋል፣ የደንበኞች ነፃነት (Consumer Sovereignty) ይከበራል፣ ሀብት በብቃት ስራ ላይ ይውላል።
• ጉዳቶቹ፦ በሀብታምና በደሃ መካከል ያለው ልዩነት ይሰፋል (Income Inequality)፣ የአካባቢ ብክለት (Negative Externalities) ይበዛል፣ የሰራተኞች ጉልበት ብዝበዛ ሊኖር ይችላል።

💡 Exam Hint: Market Mechanism vs Laissez-faire
በፈተና ላይ 'Laissez-faire' ወይም 'Invisible Hand' የሚሉ ቃላትን ካያችሁ ቀጥታ ከCapitalist / Free Market Economy ጋር የሚያያዙ መሆናቸውን እንዳትረሱ!


1.6.2 Command Economy (Socialist Economy)

A Command economy is also known as a socialistic economy. Under this economic system, the economic institutions that are engaged in production and distribution are owned and controlled by the state (government).

Main Features of Command Economy:
• Collective ownership: All means of production are owned by the society as a whole (state ownership); private property rights are absent.
• Central economic planning: Resource allocation is planned by a central controlling authority according to set socio-economic goals.
• Strong government role: Complete government control over all economic activities.
• Maximum social welfare: Aims at maximizing overall societal welfare rather than individual profits.
• Relative equality of incomes: Absence of profit motive and private accumulation reduces the income gap.

Advantages of Command Economy:
• Absence of wasteful competition: Eliminates redundant investments and unhealthy market rivalry.
• Balanced economic growth: Planned resource allocation ensures equal development across sectors and regions.
• Elimination of private monopolies & inequalities: Prevents wealth concentration in the hands of a few private individuals.

Disadvantages of Command Economy:
• Absence of automatic price determination: Lack of a price mechanism leads to inefficiencies and misallocation.
• Absence of incentives for hard work: Bureaucratic management offers little financial reward for individual effort and efficiency.
• Lack of economic freedom: Consumers and producers lose their freedom of choice.
• Red-tapism & Bureaucracy: Decision-making is slow due to excessive government paperwork and regulations.

👉 ኮማንድ/ሶሻሊስት ኢኮኖሚ (Command Economy) :
• ዋና መገለጫዎች፦ የሀገር ሀብት በሙሉ የህዝብ/የመንግስት ነው፤ የግል ንብረት የለም፤ ምንና እንዴት መመረት እንዳለበት የሚወስነው በማዕከላዊ የመንግስት እቅድ (Central Planning) ነው፤ የዋጋ አሰራር በገበያ ሳይሆን በመንግስት ይወሰናል።
• ጥቅሞቹ፦ የሀብት ማባከንና አላስፈላጊ ውድድር የለም፣ የሀብታምና ደሃ ልዩነት ይበልጥ የተጠበበ ነው፣ እኩል እድገት ለማምጣት ይመቻል።
• ጉዳቶቹ፦ የሰዎች ስራ ወኔና ትጋት ይቀንሳል (Incentive የለም)፣ ቢሮክራሲና የውሳኔ ዘግየት (Red-tapism) ይበዛል፣ የደንበኞች ምርጫ ይገደባል።


1.6.3 Mixed Economy

A mixed economy is an attempt to combine the advantages of both the capitalistic economy and the command economy. It incorporates features of both systems and allows the private and public sectors to co-exist.

Main Features of Mixed Economy:
• Co-existence of public and private sectors: Strategic industries (defense, power, heavy infrastructure) are run by the government, while consumer goods and small-scale industries are managed by private enterprises.
• Economic welfare & Price mechanism: Price mechanism operates for private sector goods, while essential public goods/services are regulated or subsidized by the government.
• Economic planning: Government utilizes macro-planning tools to coordinate rapid, balanced economic growth.
• Economic equality: Private property is permitted alongside progressive taxation and subsidies to prevent excessive wealth concentration.

Advantages of Mixed Economy:
• Combines private property incentives, profit motive, and price mechanism with government oversight to prevent exploitation.
• Ensures adequate economic freedom for consumers, workers, and producers.
• Promotes rapid, planned economic development and social welfare.

Disadvantages of Mixed Economy:
• Ineffectiveness and inefficiency: Risk of suffering from both public sector inefficiency (lack of incentive) and private sector restriction.
• Economic fluctuations & Corruption: Improper regulation can cause unemployment, black markets, and corruption.

👉 ቀላቅለሽ ኢኮኖሚ (Mixed Economy) :
• የሁለቱ ውህደት፦ የካፒታሊዝምንና የኮማንድ ኢኮኖሚን ጥሩ ጥሩ ጎኖች ያጣመረ ነው፤ የግልና የመንግስት ዘርፍ (Public & Private Sectors) ጎን ለጎን ይሰራሉ።
• የስራ ክፍፍል፦ መሠረታዊና ስትራቴጂካዊ ተቋማት (መብራት፣ መንገድ፣ መከላከያ) በመንግስት ይያዛሉ፤ የፍጆታ እቃዎችና ትናንሽ ንግዶች በግል ባለሃብቶች ይካሄዳሉ። ኢትዮጵያ የምትከተለው ይህንን የMixed Economy ሞዴል ነው!


1.7 Decision Making Units and the Circular Flow Model

There are three major decision-making units in a closed economy:

1. Household: A household can be one person or a group of people living under one roof who make joint financial decisions. Households make two key decisions:
  a) Selling their productive resources (labor, land, capital, entrepreneurship).
  b) Buying final goods and services.

2. Firm: A firm is a production unit that uses economic resources to produce goods and services. Firms make two key decisions:
  a) Buying economic resources from households.
  b) Selling finished goods and services.

3. Government: An organization that holds legal and political power to control or influence households, business firms, and markets. It provides public goods and services for society.

The Interaction Markets:
• Product Market: The market where final goods and services are transacted (households buy, firms sell).
• Factor Market (Input Market): The market where factors of production are transacted (households sell resources, firms buy).

👉 3ቱ የውሳኔ ሰጭ አካላትና ገበያዎች :
• Households (ቤተሰቦች)፦ የሀብት ባለቤቶች ናቸው፤ ጉልበትና መሬት ይሸጣሉ፣ እቃዎችን ይገዛሉ።
• Firms (ድርጅቶች)፦ ሀብት ገዝተው ምርት የሚያመርቱና የሚሸጡ ናቸው።
• Government (መንግስት)፦ ገበያውን የሚቆጣጠርና ህዝባዊ አገልግሎቶችን (Public goods) የሚያቀርብ ነው።
• Product Market፦ ያለቀላቸው እቃዎች የሚሸጡበት ገበያ ሲሆን፣ Factor Market ደግሞ የሰው ጉልበትና ካፒታል የሚሸጥበት ገበያ ነው።


The Circular Flow Model: Two-Sector vs. Three-Sector

The circular-flow diagram is a visual model of the economy that shows how money (Birr), economic resources, and goods/services flow through markets among decision-making units.

1. Two-Sector Circular Flow Model (Households & Firms):
• Real Flow (Flow of Inputs & Outputs): Represented by the outer loop (Orange). Households supply factors of production to firms through the factor market; firms use them to produce final goods and services sold to households in the product market.
• Money / Nominal Flow (Flow of Birr): Represented by the inner loop (Green). Households spend money on goods/services (spending), which becomes revenue for firms. Firms then pay wages, rent, and interest back to households.

Figure 1.4: Circular flow of income with two sector model

🔄 Two-Sector Circular Flow Breakdown:
• Top Half (Product Market): Firms sell goods/services → Households buy. Spending flows from Households to Firms; Goods flow from Firms to Households.
• Bottom Half (Factor Market): Households sell inputs → Firms buy. Payments (Wages/Rent/Interest/Profit) flow from Firms to Households; Resources flow from Households to Firms.

2. Three-Sector Circular Flow Model (Households, Firms, & Government):
The three-sector model incorporates government participation in the market economy:
• Government purchases goods/services from firms in the product market (Government Expenditure).
• Government hires resources from households in the factor market and pays factor incomes.
• Government collects Taxes from both households and business firms.
• Government provides public services, Subsidies to firms, and Income support / Social transfers to households.

Figure 1.5: Three sector circular flow of resources

👉 የኢኮኖሚ ፍሰት ሞዴል (Circular Flow Model) :
• Real Flow (እውነተኛ ፍሰት)፦ የእቃ፣ የአገልግሎትና የምርት ሀብቶች (Labor, Land) እንቅስቃሴ ነው።
• Money Flow (የገንዘብ ፍሰት)፦ የእቃ መግዣ ወጪ (Spending) እና የደሞዝ/ኪራይ/ትርፍ (Income) እንቅስቃሴ ነው።
• በ3-Sector ሞዴል ውስጥ የመንግስት ሚና፦ መንግስት ከግለሰቦችና ድርጅቶች Tax (ግብር) ይሰበስባል፤ በምላሹ ለድርጅቶች Subsidy (ድጎማ)፣ ለግለሰቦች ደግሞ Income support (የገንዘብ ድጋፍ) እና ህዝባዊ አገልግሎቶችን ይሰጣል።

💡 Exam Focus Points for Chapter 1:
• Clockwise vs Counter-clockwise: በ Two-sector model ግራፍ ላይ Real Flow (Outer Loop) Clockwise ሲሆን Money Flow (Inner Loop) ደግሞ Counter-clockwise መሆኑን አስተውሉ!
• Factors of Production & Rewards: Labor → Wage, Land → Rent, Capital → Interest, Entrepreneurship → Profit.
• PPF Concavity: Due to Increasing Opportunity Cost (Resources are not perfectly adaptable).
